applicability.basis: the calibration set's range of each listed variable (the charge state through the family's reconstruction), widened by the declared scope margins; the margins are a scope policy, not a measurement accuracy

conventions.capacity_basis: per cell: the charge delivered by that cell's 0.5 A capacity-check run
conventions.initial_polarization: 0 V at sample 0 (the run starts from a 2 h rest)
conventions.initial_state: soc = 1 at sample 0 (full charge, then rest)

declared_family.equations: V = OCV(z) - I*R0 - v1;  dv1/dt = I/C1 - v1/(R1*C1);  dz/dt = -I/Q.  Positive I is discharge.  Rint (R1 = 0) is the declared rival.

ocv.representation: piecewise-linear table on the declared knots; the knot values are latent parameters

description: Two sibling cells of one batch in a room-temperature chamber. Each run: from full charge (CC-CV, then 2 h rest), a constant-current discharge at a protocol-set rate (0.5, 2.5, 5 or 7.5 A) to the cutoff voltage, then rest; 30 s sampling; the cell self-heats at the higher rates. Calibration: cell u14's 0.5 A and 7.5 A runs. Within-cell held-out: cell u14's 2.5 A and 5 A runs. Cross-cell held-out: cell u15's 2.5 A and 5 A runs. The open-circuit voltage was not measured.

measurement_noise.basis: no accuracy statement is published for the instrument; the uncertainty is never set to zero and no residual estimate replaces it

questions.CROSS_CELL_TRANSFER: Does the calibrated family predict the cross-cell held-out set within its declared acceptance bar, inside the declared applicability domain? SUPPORTED / NOT_SUPPORTED.
questions.IDENTIFIABILITY: Are the requested parameters identifiable from the calibration observations under the declared measurement uncertainty? SUPPORTED = every requested parameter identifiable; NOT_SUPPORTED = not all identifiable.
questions.MODEL_ADEQUACY: Does the declared family, calibrated on the calibration set, describe the calibration data within the declared adequacy bar? SUPPORTED = adequate; NOT_SUPPORTED = inadequate.
questions.MODEL_DISCREPANCY: Are the calibration residuals compatible with the declared measurement uncertainty and the parameter uncertainty? SUPPORTED = compatible; NOT_SUPPORTED = model-form error resolved beyond them.
questions.WITHIN_CELL_GENERALIZATION: Does the calibrated family predict the within-cell held-out set within its declared acceptance bar, inside the declared applicability domain? SUPPORTED / NOT_SUPPORTED.
questions.set_rule: A held-out subset is judged only inside the declared applicability domain: an in-domain subset that fails its bar makes the set NOT_SUPPORTED; a subset holding any trajectory outside the domain is not scored, so the set cannot be SUPPORTED from it.
questions.vocabulary: Every answer is one of SUPPORTED, NOT_SUPPORTED, REVIEW, NOT_ASSESSABLE, REFUSED. REVIEW, NOT_ASSESSABLE and REFUSED are non-committal: they never count as support.
